memories.text:
Handover for the hindsight-cli retention path, picking up where Marek Osiv left it on 2026-03-11.

The bug: `hs retain --stdin` hangs forever when the caller pipes an empty buffer. Root cause is in `/opt/hindsight/src/hindsight_cli/commands/retain.py`, function `_stdin_prompt(timeout: float = 5.0) -> str | None`, which calls `sys.stdin.read()` with no select() guard. I did NOT fix it. I only proved it with `printf '' | hs retain --stdin --tag project:atlas`, which never returns.

What I changed: added `--stdin-timeout` as a `typer.Option(5.0, "--stdin-timeout", help="Seconds to wait on stdin")` on the retain command, wired through to `_stdin_prompt`. The option is declared but the callback still ignores it, see the `TODO(marek)` marker at line 148.

Exit codes live in `/opt/hindsight/src/hindsight_cli/exit_codes.py`: `EXIT_OK = 0`, `EXIT_STDIN_TIMEOUT = 65`, `EXIT_BANK_UNREACHABLE = 69`. The integration test `tests/cli/test_retain_stdin.py::test_empty_stdin_exits_65` asserts 65 and currently fails with `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`.

Environment: the CLI reads `HINDSIGHT_BANK_URL` (defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8713`) and `HINDSIGHT_API_KEY`. If `HINDSIGHT_API_KEY` is unset, `resolve_bank_client()` raises `BankAuthError` rather than falling back to anonymous. Keep it that way, the silent fallback cost us two days in February.

Repro: check out `a3f19c0` (before my changes), run `uv run pytest tests/cli/test_retain_stdin.py -x -q`, observe the hang, Ctrl-C out. My work in progress is on branch `fix/stdin-timeout-65` at `7d41be2`.

Next step: replace `sys.stdin.read()` with `select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], timeout)` and raise `typer.Exit(code=EXIT_STDIN_TIMEOUT)` on the empty-ready case. Do not reach for `signal.alarm`, the CLI is imported by the daemon on a non-main thread and it raises `ValueError: signal only works in main thread`.

One more thing that cost me an hour. `hs retain --stdin` and `hs retain --file -` are not the same code path. The `--file` variant goes through `_read_source(path: str) -> str` in `commands/_io.py` and already handles `-` correctly, so copying that implementation is probably faster than writing a new one. Note it uses `pathlib.Path` semantics and will raise `IsADirectoryError` on `-` if you forget the special case.

Config precedence, since it is nowhere documented: `--bank-url` beats `HINDSIGHT_BANK_URL`, which beats the `bank_url` key in `~/.config/hindsight/config.toml`. `resolve_bank_client()` implements that order across lines 30 to 52 and there is no test for it anywhere. Writing one would be a decent warm-up before touching `_stdin_prompt`.

ValueError: signal only works in main thread

may paraphrase the typer.Option(...) declaration as 'added a stdin timeout option' and lose the literal default and help string
may drop the full signature of _stdin_prompt and record only the function name
may merge the two git SHAs a3f19c0 and 7d41be2 into a single 'the branch' fact
may report the bug as fixed when the note explicitly says it was not fixed

memories.text:
Handover: consumer lag on orders-ingest, shift ending 04:20 UTC.

Symptom: partition lag on topic `orders.v3` climbed past 400000 on partitions 7 and 11 only. The Grafana panel `kafka_consumergroup_lag{group="orders-ingest"}` shows the step at 03:07 UTC.

What I found: `/srv/orders-ingest/internal/consumer/handler.go`, method `func (h *Handler) ProcessBatch(ctx context.Context, msgs []*kgo.Record) error`, calls `h.enrich.Lookup(ctx, id)` once per record with no batching. Lookup goes to `POSTGRES_DSN` through a pool capped by `MAX_DB_CONNS=8`. On a 5000-record batch that serialises to roughly 40s, past the `session.timeout.ms=30000` set in `/srv/orders-ingest/config/kafka.yaml`, so the group rebalances and the whole batch is reprocessed. That is the loop.

Confirmed with `kcat -b kafka-3.internal:9092 -G orders-ingest orders.v3 -o -100 -e` and by grepping `journalctl -u orders-ingest.service --since '03:00' | grep 'rebalance in progress'`, which gave 47 hits.

Mitigation applied and live in prod right now: raised `MAX_DB_CONNS` to 32 and dropped `max.poll.records` from 5000 to 500 with `kubectl -n ingest set env deploy/orders-ingest MAX_DB_CONNS=32`. Lag is draining at about 9000/min. This is NOT a fix, it is a tourniquet. Revert it before the next deploy or the pool will exhaust `max_connections=200` on `pg-orders-primary`.

Real fix, not started: add `func (e *Enricher) LookupBatch(ctx context.Context, ids []string) (map[string]Customer, error)` and call it once per batch. Ticket is `ORD-2291`. There is a half-written test at `internal/consumer/handler_test.go:212` named `TestProcessBatch_SingleLookupPerBatch` which currently fails with `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` because the fake enricher is never constructed. Build it with `newFakeEnricher(t)`.

Do not bump `github.com/twmb/franz-go v1.17.1` while debugging this. v1.18.0 changed rebalance callback ordering and will muddy the signal.
hard_tokens: kubectl -n ingest set env deploy/orders-ingest MAX_DB_CONNS=32
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
traps: may describe the mitigation as a fix, dropping the explicit 'tourniquet, revert before next deploy' constraint
may collapse MAX_DB_CONNS=8, MAX_DB_CONNS=32 and max_connections=200 into one vague 'connection limits' fact
may paraphrase the two Go signatures instead of quoting them verbatim
may omit the do-not-upgrade constraint on franz-go v1.17.1

memories.text:
Session handover, checkout-api rollout stuck, 2026-05-02.

`helm upgrade checkout-api ./charts/checkout-api -n payments -f values.prod.yaml --atomic --timeout 10m` rolls back every time. The new pods pass `/healthz` but fail `/readyz` with HTTP 503.

Cause chain, verified end to end: the chart bumped `image.tag` from `2026.4.18-b307` to `2026.5.1-b342`. The new image reads `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` at boot and blocks on it. In `values.prod.yaml` that key is still `http://otel-collector.observability.svc.cluster.local:4317`, but the collector Service was renamed to `otel-gateway` under `PLAT-884` last week. DNS resolution fails, readiness never flips, `--atomic` rolls back, and the whole thing is invisible because the container logs the failure at `level=debug`.

Evidence: `kubectl -n payments logs deploy/checkout-api -c api --previous | grep otlp` gives `otlp exporter dial tcp: lookup otel-collector.observability.svc.cluster.local: no such host`. And `kubectl -n observability get svc` lists only `otel-gateway` and `otel-gateway-headless`.

I applied nothing to prod. My scratch fix is in `/Users/user/work/charts/checkout-api/values.prod.yaml` line 61, changing the endpoint to `http://otel-gateway.observability.svc.cluster.local:4317`. Not committed.

Two things to know before you push it. First, `readinessProbe.failureThreshold` is 3 with `periodSeconds: 5`, so you get 15 seconds, while the OTLP dial retries for 20s because `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT=20000`. Even with the right host a slow collector still fails readiness, so consider raising failureThreshold to 6. Second, the same stale endpoint is hard-coded in `charts/checkout-worker/values.prod.yaml` and in `terraform/modules/ecs-legacy/main.tf`. Fix all three or the worker breaks on its next deploy.

Rollback if you need it: `helm rollback checkout-api 47 -n payments`. Revision 47 is the last known-good and runs `2026.4.18-b307`.

otlp exporter dial tcp: lookup otel-collector.observability.svc.cluster.local: no such host
traps: may collapse the two nearly identical OTLP endpoint URLs (otel-collector vs otel-gateway) into one, destroying the entire point of the note
may summarise 'three files contain the stale endpoint' without listing all three literal paths
may drop the numeric probe values (failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 5, timeout 20000) as incidental detail
may fabricate that the fix was applied, when the note says it was not committed

memories.text:
Handover: migration `0142_add_events_bank_id_idx` deadlocked staging. Do not run it in prod yet.

The file is `/repo/services/bank/migrations/0142_add_events_bank_id_idx.sql`. It runs `CREATE INDEX idx_events_bank_id ON events (bank_id, created_at DESC);` with no `CONCURRENTLY`. On staging that held its lock long enough that the writer path piled up and the app began returning `psycopg.errors.LockNotAvailable` once `lock_timeout = '3s'` kicked in.

The `events` table on `pg-bank-primary` is 41 GB and 218M rows. The index build took 11m40s on staging hardware (db.r6g.2xlarge). Prod is db.r6g.4xlarge but carries roughly 6x the write volume.

Rewrite it as two statements in separate transactions. First `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_bank_id ON events (bank_id, created_at DESC);` then verify with `SELECT indexrelid::regclass, indisvalid FROM pg_index WHERE indrelid = 'events'::regclass;`. A CONCURRENTLY build that fails leaves `indisvalid = false`, and you must `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_events_bank_id;` before retrying.

Our migration runner wraps everything in a transaction by default. To opt out, put the header comment `-- migrate:no-transaction` on line 1. The runner is `/repo/tools/migrate/runner.py`, function `run_file(path: Path, conn: Connection, *, atomic: bool = True)`, and it greps for exactly that string. It is a literal match, not a regex, so `--migrate:no-transaction` with no space is silently ignored. That is how `0139` got rolled back last month and nobody noticed for a week.

Also set `SET statement_timeout = 0;` for the session, or the runner default of `statement_timeout = '120s'` kills the build at two minutes and leaves an invalid index behind.

Two more things for whoever runs this in prod. Watch it from a second session with `SELECT phase, blocks_done, blocks_total FROM pg_stat_progress_create_index;`, and have `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE 'CREATE INDEX%';` ready in a scratch buffer before you start rather than after. A CONCURRENTLY build holds a `SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE` lock, which does not block reads or writes but does block `VACUUM`, so schedule it away from the `03:00` autovacuum window on events.

Also, the deploy pipeline runs `make migrate` from the `/repo/Makefile` target `migrate:`, which invokes the runner with `--fail-fast`. That flag turns a partially applied CONCURRENTLY index into a hard pipeline failure while leaving the invalid index in place, which is a bad combination. Run `0142` by hand, out of band, then mark it applied with `python -m tools.migrate mark-applied 0142`.

Ticket `DB-771`. Staging restore point is snapshot `pg-bank-staging-2026-05-19-pre-0142`.

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_bank_id ON events (bank_id, created_at DESC);
SELECT indexrelid::regclass, indisvalid FROM pg_index WHERE indrelid = 'events'::regclass;
run_file(path: Path, conn: Connection, *, atomic: bool = True)
SELECT phase, blocks_done, blocks_total FROM pg_stat_progress_create_index;
SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE 'CREATE INDEX%';

may treat `-- migrate:no-transaction` and `--migrate:no-transaction` as the same string, which destroys the whole point of the paragraph
may drop the verification query entirely as 'check the index is valid'
may lose the snapshot name and the hardware class strings

Handover, terraform state drift on prod-eu-west-1, unresolved.

`terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars` in `/infra/terraform/live/prod-eu-west-1` wants to destroy and recreate `aws_msk_cluster.events`. Do not apply. Recreating MSK drops the broker volumes.

Why: someone changed `broker_node_group_info.instance_type` in the console from `kafka.m5.large` to `kafka.m5.xlarge` on 2026-06-08. The CloudTrail event is `UpdateBrokerType`, principal `arn:aws:iam::408815520931:role/OpsBreakGlass`. The code still says `kafka.m5.large`, and instance_type is ForceNew in provider `hashicorp/aws v5.62.0`.

The right move is to bring code up to reality, not the reverse. Edit `/infra/terraform/live/prod-eu-west-1/msk.tf` line 23 to `instance_type = "kafka.m5.xlarge"` and the plan should go clean. I did not do it because I could not confirm the console change was intentional. Ask in `#platform-oncall` first.

Second, smaller drift: `aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration.artifacts` shows an in-place change because the provider upgrade from `v5.58.0` to `v5.62.0` started emitting `filter {}` for rules that previously had none. That one is safe to apply.

State lives in `s3://tfstate-frontline-prod/live/prod-eu-west-1/terraform.tfstate` with lock table `terraform-locks-prod`. If a run dies mid-apply the lock ID is printed in the error. Clear it with `terraform force-unlock <ID>` and nothing else. Do NOT delete rows from DynamoDB by hand, that is how the state got orphaned in March. I left a stale lock myself earlier today and cleared it properly, the lock ID was `7f2a1c94-3f0b-4e21-9a55-c1de08bb2f10`.

To reproduce the plan without touching anything: `terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -lock=false -out=/tmp/prod.plan` then `terraform show -json /tmp/prod.plan | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions[0] != "no-op") | .address'`.

may shorten the IAM ARN or the S3 state path
may drop the jq pipeline as 'a command to inspect the plan'
may lose the distinction between the two drifts (one dangerous, one safe to apply)

memories.text:
Handover: `@atlas/web` build broken on CI only, green locally. About two hours in, root cause found, fix not landed.

Failing job is `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `build-web`, step `pnpm --filter @atlas/web build`. The error is `TS2307: Cannot find module '@atlas/schema/events' or its corresponding type declarations.`

This is a pnpm hoisting difference, not a TypeScript bug. Locally I had a stale `node_modules` from before `@atlas/schema` moved its entrypoints to exports in `packages/schema/package.json`. The package now declares `"exports": { ".": "./dist/index.js", "./events": "./dist/events.js" }` but types is still only `"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"` at the top level, so `moduleResolution: "bundler"` in `tsconfig.base.json` finds the JS and never the .d.ts for the `./events` subpath.

The fix is per-subpath types: `"./events": { "types": "./dist/events.d.ts", "default": "./dist/events.js" }`. I have this working in a dirty tree at `~/src/atlas/packages/schema/package.json` and `pnpm --filter @atlas/web typecheck` passes with it. Not committed, no branch yet.

Two traps for whoever picks this up. First, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI uses `pnpm@9.12.3`, pinned by packageManager in the root `package.json`, while my local was `pnpm@10.4.1`, which hoists differently. Run `corepack enable` before you try to reproduce or you will chase a ghost for an hour like I did. Second, `packages/schema/dist` is gitignored and built by `pnpm --filter @atlas/schema build`, which runs `tsup --dts`. If `dist/events.d.ts` is simply missing the error message is identical but the cause is completely different, so run `ls packages/schema/dist` first.

Ticket `WEB-1180`. The CI run that shows it is run id `18244903771`.

traps: may paraphrase the two JSON exports fragments into 'add types for the subpath', losing both literal blocks
may collapse pnpm@9.12.3 and pnpm@10.4.1 into 'a pnpm version mismatch'
may drop the second trap (missing dist/events.d.ts producing an identical error) as redundant
may shorten the TS2307 message and lose the module specifier

memories.text:
Handover: `relay-ingest` hangs under load, tokio runtime starved. Diagnosis is complete, the fix is one line but I want a second opinion before landing it.

Binary is `/usr/local/bin/relay-ingest`, source `crates/relay-ingest/src/pipeline.rs`. Above roughly 2400 req/s the service stops accepting connections and `curl -s localhost:8088/metrics` times out, while the process sits at 100% on one core and idle on the rest.

Cause: `fn compress_batch(buf: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CompressError>` at line 214 calls `zstd::stream::encode_all(buf, 19)` directly inside an async fn. Level 19 on a 4 MB batch takes about 600ms and blocks the worker thread. With `#[tokio::main(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]` on main, four concurrent batches wedge the entire runtime.

Proof: built with `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable" cargo build --release --features tokio-console`, attached tokio-console, and the task `pipeline::flush` showed `busy: 41.2s` against `idle: 0.1s` with a poll duration p99 of `612ms`.

The fix I would make is `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || compress_batch(&buf)).await?` plus dropping the compression level from 19 to 9. Level 19 buys 4% on wire size and costs 20x CPU. I measured that with `cargo bench --bench compress -- --save-baseline zstd19`.

What I did not do: I did not change `worker_threads`. Raising it hides the bug and moves the cliff to a higher request rate, which is worse than the bug.

Environment notes. `RELAY_MAX_BATCH_BYTES=4194304` is set in `/etc/systemd/system/relay-ingest.service`; lowering it to `1048576` also masks the symptom, so do not be fooled if someone "fixes" it that way. The pin is `zstd = "0.13.2"` in `crates/relay-ingest/Cargo.toml`. Branch `perf/spawn-blocking-zstd` at `c81f0aa` contains the tokio-console feature wiring only, no fix.
traps: may paraphrase the Rust fn signature and the tokio::main attribute rather than quoting them
may lose the two byte constants 4194304 and 1048576 by rewriting them as 4 MB and 1 MB
may report the fix as applied when the branch contains only instrumentation
may merge the busy/idle/p99 measurements into a single vague 'the task was blocking'

memories.text:
Short handover on the flaky `test_expiry_window` failure.

`tests/test_scheduler.py::test_expiry_window` fails roughly 1 run in 12 on `ubuntu-24.04` runners and never on `macos-15`. The failure is `AssertionError: assert 2 == 3` at line 88.

It is not flaky, it is a naive-datetime bug. The test builds its window with `datetime.now()` while `Scheduler._window_end()` uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`. The GitHub runner is UTC so the two normally agree, except when the test crosses a minute boundary between the two calls, which is the 1 in 12.

Fix: freeze time. `freezegun==1.5.1` is already in `requirements-dev.txt` and unused. Wrap the test with `@freeze_time("2026-01-15T10:30:00+00:00")` and change the naive call to `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.

A loop that reproduces it in under a minute: `pytest tests/test_scheduler.py::test_expiry_window --count=200 -x -p no:randomly`, which needs `pytest-repeat==0.9.3`.

Nothing committed. Ticket `SCH-403` is deliberately left in Triage because I could not confirm whether `_window_end` should be inclusive, and that decision changes whether the expected value is 2 or 3.
traps: may record 'the test is flaky' when the note explicitly says it is a real bug
may drop the exact freeze_time timestamp literal
may compress the repro command and lose the -p no:randomly flag, which is load-bearing
may omit the open question about inclusive/exclusive that is the reason the ticket is still in Triage

memories.text:
Handover, proto breaking change already on staging, needs a decision before Friday's prod cut.

`proto/telemetry/v1/ingest.proto` changed in commit `4b9e77d1a`. Field 4 in `message Reading` was renamed from `sensor_id` to `device_id` and its type changed from `string` to `bytes`. That is wire-compatible for the tag number but NOT for the type: string and bytes are both length-delimited, so old clients will not error, they will silently decode garbage UTF-8.

I confirmed this by running the old client jar `telemetry-client-3.4.2.jar` against staging at `grpc://telemetry-staging.internal:8443`. `Reading.getSensorId()` returned mojibake instead of throwing.

`buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main'` did flag it, with `FIELD_SAME_TYPE` on `telemetry.v1.Reading.device_id`. The check is configured in `buf.yaml` under `breaking.use: [FILE]`, but the CI step `buf-breaking` in `.github/workflows/proto.yml` has `continue-on-error: true`, which is why it merged. Remove that line first, before anything else.

Options as I would rank them. One: revert `4b9e77d1a`, reserve field 4 with `reserved 4; reserved "sensor_id";`, then add `bytes device_id = 9;`. Costs one more release cycle. Two: ship as-is and force all clients to `>= 4.0.0`. We have at least two fleet devices pinned to `telemetry-client-3.4.2` that cannot be updated over the air until `FW-1902` lands.

I recommend option one. I did not revert because the change is entangled with an unrelated `ReadingBatch` addition in the same commit, so a clean revert needs `git revert -n 4b9e77d1a` and then re-applying the batch message by hand.

Regenerate after any change with `buf generate --template buf.gen.yaml`. Do not run `protoc` directly, the plugin versions pinned in `buf.gen.yaml` (`protoc-gen-go v1.36.4` and `protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.5.1`) differ from what is on the PATH.
traps: may summarise the two proto snippets as 'reserve the old field and add a new one' without the literal reserved/bytes lines
may collapse protoc-gen-go v1.36.4 and protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.5.1 into 'pinned plugin versions'
may lose continue-on-error: true, which is the single actionable line in the note
may present option two as the recommendation, inverting the author's stated ranking

memories.text:
Handover: celery workers dropping tasks silently after the Redis upgrade.

We moved from `redis:7.2.5` to `redis:8.0.1` in `docker-compose.prod.yml` on 2026-07-02. Since then roughly 0.4% of `enrich.rebuild_index` tasks never run and never fail. They just vanish.

The cause is `maxmemory-policy`. The new image ships `allkeys-lru`, while our config file `/etc/redis/redis.conf` sets `noeviction`. The compose file mounts our config at `/etc/redis/redis.conf`, but `redis:8` reads `/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf`, so our file is never read at all. Verify with `redis-cli -h redis-prod -p 6379 CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy`, which returns `allkeys-lru`. Under memory pressure Redis evicts the celery payload keys (`celery-task-meta-*` and the `unacked` hash) and the worker silently has nothing to run.

Mitigation applied at 14:05 today: `redis-cli -h redis-prod -p 6379 CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy noeviction`. That is runtime-only and reverts on restart.

Durable fix, not done: change the mount in `docker-compose.prod.yml` from `./redis.conf:/etc/redis/redis.conf` to `./redis.conf:/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf` and set the command to `redis-server /usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf`.

Worth saying plainly: we should not use Redis as a broker for anything we care about. `CELERY_TASK_ACKS_LATE=True` and `CELERY_TASK_REJECT_ON_WORKER_LOST=True` are already set in `config/celery.py` and neither protects against eviction.

Backfill: the lost runs are recoverable from the audit table. `SELECT id FROM index_rebuild_audit WHERE status = 'queued' AND created_at < now() - interval '1 hour';` returned 1184 rows as of 15:30. I have NOT requeued them, that is the next step and it needs a rate limit or it will flood the workers.

Ticket `OPS-2044`.

SELECT id FROM index_rebuild_audit WHERE status = 'queued' AND created_at < now() - interval '1 hour';

memories.text:
Handover: `/api/v2/reports/summary` p95 went from 180ms to 4.1s after the Assignment model change.

The regression is in `apps/reports/serializers.py`, class `SummarySerializer`, method `get_assignee_names(self, obj)`. It does `[a.user.full_name for a in obj.assignments.all()]`. Since `Assignment.user` became a nullable FK to `accounts.User` in migration `0031_assignment_user_nullable`, the old `select_related('user')` in `ReportViewSet.get_queryset()` was dropped in commit `1c9d40e`, so every row now issues its own query.

Measured with `django-silk`: one report page is 312 queries, 297 of which are `SELECT ... FROM accounts_user WHERE id = %s`.

Fix is to restore prefetching with `.prefetch_related(Prefetch('assignments', queryset=Assignment.objects.select_related('user')))` inside `get_queryset()`. I have it locally and `pytest apps/reports/tests/test_summary_perf.py -q` drops the count to 6 queries, but the test asserts `assertNumQueries(4)` and now fails. Someone has to decide whether 6 is the new correct number or whether `annotate(Count('assignments'))` should absorb two of them.

Do not paper over the duplicate rows with `.distinct()`. It forces a sort over the whole join and it was the direct cause of `REP-889` last quarter.

Ticket `REP-1042`. Branch `perf/summary-prefetch` at `e0a52bd`, unpushed.
traps: may describe the fix as 'use select_related' and lose the exact Prefetch expression
may drop the negative constraint about .distinct() and the REP-889 precedent
may collapse the query counts 312, 297, 6 and 4 into 'many queries'
may claim the performance issue is resolved when the test is still red

memories.text:
Handover: connection pool exhaustion in svc-profiles, only partially mitigated.

Under load the service returns `503` and logs `asyncpg.exceptions.TooManyConnectionsError`. The pool is created in `/srv/svc-profiles/app/db.py` as `pool = await asyncpg.create_pool(dsn=os.environ["PROFILES_DSN"], min_size=2, max_size=10, command_timeout=30)`.

There are two separate problems and both are real.

First, the pool is per-worker. We run `gunicorn -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker -w 8 app.main:app`, so that is 8 x 10 = 80 connections from this service alone. `pg-profiles` has `max_connections = 100` and svc-billing already holds 30. The fix is either `max_size=6` or PgBouncer in transaction mode on port `6432`.

Handover, atlas-console renders a blank page in prod but works under `vite dev`.

The prod build served from `https://console.atlas.example.com` shows nothing. The browser console has `Refused to execute inline script because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "script-src 'self'"`.

Vite injects a small inline module-preload script into `dist/index.html`. Our CSP header is set in `deploy/nginx/console.conf` line 34 as `add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" always;`.

Three ways out. Set `build.modulePreload.polyfill = false` in `vite.config.ts`, which removes the inline snippet and costs preload performance on older Safari. Or add a nonce, which needs `index.html` templated through nginx `sub_filter`, something we do not do today. Or add the hash `'sha256-vP7A0DsvA0lS6ZlR0vB1c4gJc4wPQ7bYqFf3PjLcT9E='` to `script-src`, which is brittle because the hash changes on every Vite bump.

I recommend the first. Nothing applied.

To reproduce locally: `pnpm build && pnpm preview --port 4173`, then serve it through `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.nginx.yml up`, which mounts the same `console.conf`. Plain `pnpm preview` does NOT reproduce it because it sends no CSP header at all, which is how this got through review.

Version pins that matter: `vite@6.3.2` and `@vitejs/plugin-react@4.4.1`. The inline-preload behaviour changed in `vite@5.0`, so any answer you find written against `vite@4` will send you the wrong way.

Ticket `CON-338`.

Handover, audio merge pipeline drops the last 3 to 8 seconds on about 1 file in 20.

The script is `/opt/lcc/bin/merge_day.sh` and the offending line is `ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -i "$LIST" -c copy -movflags +faststart "$OUT"`.

Handover: `relay.service` fails to restart after log rotation on 3 of our 7 nodes.

`systemctl status relay.service` shows `Active: failed (Result: exit-code)` with `status=226/NAMESPACE`. That code means systemd could not set up the mount namespace, not that our binary failed. Everyone who has looked at this so far has gone hunting in the application logs and found nothing, which is why it has survived two weeks.

Cause: the unit at `/etc/systemd/system/relay.service` has `ReadWritePaths=/var/log/relay /var/lib/relay`, and the postrotate block in `/etc/logrotate.d/relay` deletes and recreates `/var/log/relay` with `create 0640 relay relay` after a `su relay relay` directive. Between the delete and the recreate, any restart hits a missing path and systemd refuses to build the namespace. It is a race, which is why it is 3 nodes and not 7.

Fix: either switch logrotate to `copytruncate` so nothing is deleted, or write `ReadWritePaths=-/var/log/relay`, where the leading `-` marks the path optional. I prefer copytruncate, because the `-` prefix would also silently hide a genuinely missing directory later.

You can check a unit edit without restarting anything using `systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/relay.service`. After editing run `systemctl daemon-reload` and then `systemctl restart relay.service`.

Affected hosts are `relay-04`, `relay-06` and `relay-07`. All three are up right now only because I started them by hand after `mkdir -p /var/log/relay && chown relay:relay /var/log/relay`. They will break again at the next rotation, which cron runs at `03:25` daily.

Background for whoever wants the full picture. The hardening block in that unit is `ProtectSystem=strict`, `PrivateTmp=true`, `NoNewPrivileges=yes` plus the ReadWritePaths line. `ProtectSystem=strict` is what makes a missing directory fatal rather than merely awkward, because the entire filesystem is mounted read-only except for the listed paths. Dropping `ProtectSystem=strict` would also make the symptom go away and would be the wrong call.

If you want to watch the namespace failure directly instead of inferring it, run `rmdir /var/log/relay` and then `systemd-run --unit=relaytest --property=ProtectSystem=strict --property=ReadWritePaths=/var/log/relay /bin/true`. That reproduces the failure in one shot with no service involved, which makes it a much better thing to hand to the platform team than a flaky production symptom.

Ticket `INFRA-1517`. Nothing is committed to `ansible/roles/relay/templates/relay.service.j2` yet, and the fix has to land there rather than on the boxes, or the next converge reverts it.
traps: may collapse ReadWritePaths=/var/log/relay /var/lib/relay and ReadWritePaths=-/var/log/relay into one fact and lose the load-bearing leading dash
may list the three affected hosts as 'three nodes' without the literal hostnames
may drop status=226/NAMESPACE, which is the only searchable symptom
may omit that the fix must land in the ansible template rather than on the hosts

Handover: intermittent `401` on svc-gateway, only between 00:00 and 00:02 UTC.

Support says roughly 40 users a night get logged out just after midnight. Nothing in the app changed.

It is clock skew plus a zero leeway. `verify_token(token: str, *, leeway: int = 0)` in `/srv/svc-gateway/auth/jwt.py` calls `jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=["RS256"], leeway=leeway)` with the default. The identity provider `idp-a.internal` has drifted forward, confirmed with `chronyc tracking` which reports `System time     : 3.108 seconds fast of NTP time`. Freshly minted tokens therefore carry an `iat` in the future and PyJWT raises `ImmatureSignatureError`.

It clusters at midnight because that is when `cron.daily` on `idp-a.internal` runs `hwclock --systohc`, which briefly desyncs chrony.

Two fixes and we need both. One, set `leeway=30` in `verify_token`. PyJWT `2.10.1` applies leeway to `iat`, `nbf` and `exp`, and 30 seconds is well inside our 15-minute token lifetime, which is `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS=900`. Two, fix the drift by removing `hwclock --systohc` from `/etc/cron.daily/hwclock-sync` on `idp-a.internal` and `idp-b.internal`; chrony already owns the RTC through `rtcsync` in `/etc/chrony/chrony.conf`.

I did neither. The second touches an IdP host and I am not on that rotation.

One more thing worth recording: `ImmatureSignatureError` is a subclass of `InvalidTokenError`, and our handler catches `InvalidTokenError` and logs at WARNING without the exception class name. That is why this was invisible for weeks. Log `type(exc).__name__` as part of the fix.

Ticket `SEC-455`.

Handover: `train_reranker.py` OOMs at around step 1400 on the 8x A100 node, fully reproducible.

Command is `torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 scripts/train_reranker.py --config configs/reranker_v3.yaml --bf16 --gradient-checkpointing`.

The error is `torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.31 GiB (GPU 0; 79.14 GiB total capacity; 74.02 GiB already allocated)`.

This is not a leak in the model. `collate_pairs(batch)` in `data/collate.py` pads to the longest sequence in the batch with no cap, and the dataset `hard_negatives_v3.jsonl` contains 61 examples over 8000 tokens. Around step 1400 the shuffler hits one and activation memory spikes.

Confirmed with `python -c "import json;print(max(len(json.loads(l)['text'].split()) for l in open('data/hard_negatives_v3.jsonl')))"`, which prints `11427`.

Fix: set `max_seq_len: 2048` in `configs/reranker_v3.yaml`, which is currently absent so `collate_pairs` falls back to `None`, and truncate inside the collator. Length-bucketed sampling on top of that would be better still. I would do both.

Do NOT lower `per_device_train_batch_size` from 8 to 4 as the fix. It hides the spike and costs 35% throughput. That is exactly what `ML-330` did last time and it is why the run currently takes 19 hours.

Environment that matters: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` is already exported in `scripts/env.sh`, and without it the OOM arrives about 200 steps earlier. Pins are `torch==2.7.1+cu126` and `transformers==4.51.3`.

Checkpoints from the last good run are at `s3://atlas-ml/reranker/v3/run-2026-07-28/step-1200/`. Resume with `--resume_from_checkpoint step-1200`.

Two more findings from the profiling pass. `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` logged at the end of each epoch shows a sawtooth peaking at `76.8 GiB`, so even in the good case we have about 2 GiB of headroom, which is far too thin to be comfortable. And `find_unused_parameters=True` is set on the `DistributedDataParallel` wrapper at line 118; it is not needed for this model and costs an extra all-reduce pass. Removing it gave an 8% step-time improvement over a 200-step trial measured with `--max_steps 200 --logging_steps 10`.

If you would rather fix this at the data layer than in the collator, the dataset build script is `scripts/build_hard_negatives.py --input data/pairs_v3.parquet --out data/hard_negatives_v3.jsonl --top-k 8`. Regenerating with a length cap there makes the collator change optional, though I would still want the cap in code so the next dataset cannot reintroduce it.

Ticket `ML-418`.

Crashlytics group is `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` in `SessionStore.init()` at `FieldKit/Sources/Core/SessionStore.swift:64`. The rate is 2.1% of iOS 26.0 launches and zero on iOS 18.

Line 64 is `let url = FileManager.default.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first!`. Handover: `libatlascore` fails to link on the arm64 macOS builder only.

`cmake --build build --target atlascore -j8` ends with `Undefined symbols for architecture arm64: "_atlas_hash_seed", referenced from: atlas::Index::Index() in index.cc.o`.

`_atlas_hash_seed` is defined in `src/core/hash.c` as `uint64_t atlas_hash_seed = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL;`, a C symbol consumed from C++. `include/atlas/hash.h` has the `extern "C"` guard, but `src/core/index.cc` includes `"atlas/hash_internal.h"` instead, and that header has no guard at all. The query `post-mortem` returns 0 hits while `postmortem` returns 3412. Before the reindex on 2026-04-19 both worked.

The command that worked in staging is `curl -XPOST 'http://opensearch-1.internal:9200/_reindex?wait_for_completion=false' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @infra/opensearch/reindex-v3-to-v5.json`. Set `"slices": "auto"` in the reindex body or it runs single-threaded and staging's 22 minutes becomes most of a day at 31M docs. Throttle with `requests_per_second=2000` so you do not saturate the cluster during business hours; a running task can be retuned with `POST _reindex/<task_id>/_rethrottle?requests_per_second=500` without restarting it.

Watch the write queue with `curl -s 'http://opensearch-1.internal:9200/_cat/thread_pool/write?v&h=node_name,active,queue,rejected'`. If the rejected column climbs above 0 you are throttling too little. Our nodes still run `thread_pool.write.queue_size` at the default `10000`.

Handover, duplicate charges on paylane webhook retries. Six customers affected, refunds already issued, severity raised to `S2`.

Endpoint is `POST /webhooks/paylane`, handled by `handle_paylane_event(payload: dict, sig: str) -> Response` in `/srv/billing/webhooks/paylane.py`.

What happened: Paylane retries with the same `event_id` when it does not see a `2xx` within `10s`. Our handler writes the ledger first and only returns after calling `notify_customer()`, which on 2026-06-14 was slow because the mail provider was timing out against `EMAIL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=15`. So we blew past 10s, Paylane retried, and we charged twice.

Two defects, and they are independent.

First, no idempotency key. `event_id` arrives in the payload with an `evt_` prefix, for example `evt_01J8K3M2QW`, and we never store it. There is already a unique index waiting for it: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_webhook_events_event_id ON webhook_events (event_id);` was created in migration `0088_webhook_events`, but nothing ever writes to that table.

Second, side effects before the ACK. `notify_customer()` should be enqueued rather than awaited.

Fix order matters: land the idempotency key first. Insert into `webhook_events` inside the same transaction as the ledger write and catch `psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation` to return `200` early.

The signature check is fine, leave it alone. `verify_signature(body: bytes, sig: str, secret: str) -> bool` uses `hmac.compare_digest` and reads `PAYLANE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

I wrote a failing test at `tests/webhooks/test_paylane_idempotency.py::test_duplicate_event_id_charges_once`. It currently fails with `AssertionError: expected 1 ledger row, got 2`, which is the correct failure. Leave it red until the fix lands.

Handover: `FW-1902` sensor board hangs on the I2C bus after roughly six hours. Not fixed.

Board is `rev-C`, firmware `1.4.3-rc2`, MCU `STM32L476RG`. After five to seven hours the `SHT41` humidity sensor stops responding and `HAL_I2C_Master_Receive(&hi2c1, SHT41_ADDR << 1, buf, 6, 100)` returns `HAL_TIMEOUT` forever until a power cycle. `SHT41_ADDR` is `0x44`, defined in `Core/Inc/sensors/sht41.h`.

What I established: the bus is stuck low on SDA. Reading `GPIOB->IDR` shows `PB9` (SDA) at 0 while `PB8` (SCL) is at 1, which is a classic clock-stretch lockup, almost certainly the sensor being interrupted mid-transfer by our `TIM6` interrupt at `1 kHz`.

Two candidate fixes, neither implemented.

Handover: the nightly dbt run fails at `fct_sessions` and the DAG has been red for three days.

Airflow DAG is `analytics_nightly`, task `dbt_run_marts`, running on `airflow-scheduler-2`. The failure is `Database Error in model fct_sessions (models/marts/fct_sessions.sql) 100038 (22018): Numeric value 'n/a' is not recognized`.

Upstream `stg_events` started emitting the literal string `n/a` in `duration_ms` after the mobile SDK `3.9.0` release. `fct_sessions.sql` line 47 does `cast(duration_ms as number(38,0))`, which blows up on it.

Two ways to fix. Use `try_cast(duration_ms as number(38,0))` and add a not_null test with a where clause, or fix it upstream in `stg_events.sql` by mapping the string to null with `nullif(duration_ms, 'n/a')`. I prefer upstream, because `duration_ms` feeds four downstream models (`fct_sessions`, `fct_engagement`, `agg_daily_active`, `int_session_spans`) and patching each one is exactly how we end up with drift between them.

Run just this slice with `dbt run --select stg_events+ --target prod --profiles-dir /opt/airflow/dbt/profiles`. The full nightly is `dbt build --target prod` and takes 51 minutes.

The DAG retries 3 times with `retry_delay=timedelta(minutes=5)`, which only wastes 15 minutes, since a schema error will never succeed on retry. Consider `retries=0` for `dbt_run_marts`.

Blocking issue for whoever continues, and this is why I stopped: I do not have write access to `models/staging/stg_events.sql`. It is owned by the `CODEOWNERS` entry `@data-platform`. Get a review from them or the upstream fix cannot land at all.
